name: Pierre-Philippe Rey
evidence: Bibliography: thèse 'Les concepts de l'anthropologie économique marxiste. Critique et mise à l'épreuve', Paris V, 1978, 'sous la direction de Louis-Vincent Thomas'.
notes: This is the 1978 (État-level) thesis. Any earlier 3e cycle thesis on Congo was not checked.

name: Michel Callon
evidence: Sources describe him as ingénieur civil des Mines with a postgraduate diploma in economics; none mention a doctorate or thesis of his own.
notes: He may never have held a doctorate (CNRS profile: 'devenu ingénieur et diplômé en économie'), but no source says so outright, so no_doctoral_advisor was not used.

name: Anne-Marie Guillemard
evidence: Sudoc record on Touraine's Persée page: 'La retraite : entre le travail et la mort : étude sociologique des comportements des retraités' / Anne-Marie Guillemard ; sous la direction de Alain Touraine, 1971.
notes: Published in 1972 as 'La retraite, une mort sociale'. French Wikipedia also calls her 'Élève d'Alain Touraine'. Institution taken from a secondary citation.

name: Charles Westoff
evidence: PAA oral history: 'Dorothy Thomas had been my major professor at Penn'; dissertation analyzed 1941 Indianapolis Fertility Study data.
notes: Clyde Kiser (Milbank) supplied the Indianapolis Study data for the thesis topic; he was not the advisor.

name: Catherine Paradeise
phd_institution: Université Paris Descartes (3e cycle); Paris IV (thèse d'État)
evidence: 1974 thèse de 3e cycle at Paris Descartes 'sous la direction du démographe Alain Girard'; ten years later 'une thèse d'État supervisée par Raymond Boudon' at Paris IV.
notes: These are not co-advisors. Girard supervised the 1974 3e cycle thesis; Boudon supervised the thèse d'État (about 1984). The reviewer should choose which one the lineage uses.

name: Erhard Friedberg
evidence: Dr. phil. (political science), FU Berlin, 1979, thesis 'Staat und Industrie in Frankreich', magna cum laude. No supervisor named.
notes: He co-authored with Michel Crozier, but no source names Crozier (or anyone else) as dissertation supervisor. Habilitation at Paris IV in 1992.

name: Christopher S. Jencks
evidence: Received a master's degree from the Harvard Graduate School of Education 'but never obtained a Ph.D.'; became a full professor of sociology at Harvard without one.
notes: His only graduate degree was the Ed.M. from HGSE.

name: Alain Caillé
evidence: Wikipedia: prepared a thesis on 'la planification comme idéologie de la bureaucratie' under Raymond Aron; later an economics doctorate and a doctorat d'État ès lettres (sociologie), directors not named.
notes: Possible lead: Raymond Aron. It is unclear whether the Aron thesis was completed or which degree it was for, and no director is given for the economics doctorate or the thèse d'État.

name: Stanley Aronowitz
evidence: PhD Union Graduate School 1975, thesis 'Marxism, Technology and Labor' (ProQuest 302786098). No advisor or committee named.
notes: Union's nontraditional program used committees. The dissertation front matter (ProQuest) might name them.

name: Pierre Fougeyrollas
evidence: Maitron: 'Il rédigea une thèse en sociologie politique sous la direction de Jean Stoetzel'; thèse d'État published 1963 as 'La Conscience politique dans la France contemporaine'.
notes: Maitron returned 403 to direct fetch; the quote comes from a search-engine extract of that page. The year is the publication year; the defence date was not confirmed.

name: Judith Lorber
evidence: PhD NYU 1971; dissertation on surgical patients and the sick role ('Going under the knife'), done on an NIH fellowship at Montefiore Hospital. No advisor named.
notes: Eliot Freidson (NYU) is a plausible guess but no source checked confirms it. Check the dissertation front matter.

name: Setsuko Nishi
evidence: PhD Chicago 1963, 'Japanese American Achievement in Chicago: A Cultural Response to Degradation'. No dissertation chair named in Wikipedia, Densho or obituaries.
notes: William Caudill (research collaborator) and Emory Bogardus (USC undergraduate mentor) are mentioned, but not as advisor. A Densho oral history PDF exists but was not read.

name: Daniel Pécaut
evidence: Sudoc record on Touraine's Persée page: 'Classe ouvrière et système politique en Colombie : 1930-1953' / Daniel Pécaut, under Touraine's direction, 1979.
notes: Probably his thèse d'État. Any earlier 3e cycle thesis was not checked. Identity fits the Latin Americanist students.

name: François Gresle
evidence: Sudoc: 'Indépendants et petits patrons : pérennité et transformations d'une classe sociale', 'préparée sous la direction de M. le professeur Alain Girard' (1978; ANRT reproduction Lille III 1980).
notes: Thèse d'État. Sudoc has 1978 and 1980 records for the same work.

name: Remi Lenoir
evidence: Sudoc: 'Transformations des rapports entre générations et apparition du troisième âge' [sous la direction de Pierre Bourdieu], 1977; also 1985 EHESS work under Bourdieu.
notes: Two works under Bourdieu: 1977 (probably the 3e cycle thesis; institution not given) and 1985 'Sécurité sociale et l'évolution des formes de codification des structures familiales' (EHESS, probably the thèse d'État). Persée does not label either explicitly as a thesis.

name: Gérard Mauger
evidence: theses.fr, Persée and CESSP list only theses he directed or examined; no record of his own thesis or its director found.
notes: He is close to Bourdieu ('Avec Bourdieu'), but that is not evidence of supervision.

name: Robert W. Hodge
evidence: No obituary, CV or dissertation record found naming his doctoral supervisor.
notes: Reed College alumnus ('59), then University of Chicago/NORC (occupational prestige work with Siegel and Rossi). The PAA memorial for Karen Oppenheim Mason says she studied with him at Chicago.

name: Karen Oppenheim
evidence: PAA memorial: graduate school at Chicago, where she studied with Robert (Bill) Hodge and James Davis; dissertation 'Voting in Recent American Presidential Elections' (1970).
notes: She is Karen Oppenheim Mason (1942-2024). Hodge is a strong lead (Reed obituary: 'worked with Robert Bill Hodge'), but he is not named as dissertation advisor. Data problems: approx_phd_year 1946 is wrong (about 1970), and William M. Mason was her then-husband, so check whether the Oppenheim to W. M. Mason student edge is real.

name: Claudine Sagaert
evidence: theses.fr: 'Généalogie de la laideur', Claudine Sagaert, Strasbourg 2011, thèse dirigée par David Le Breton (also Wikidata P184).
notes: Reversed edge in our data. David Le Breton is listed as her known_student, but he was her thesis director. The Sagaert to Le Breton link (and the 49 descendants that flow through it) should be inverted or removed.

name: Stephan P. Spitzer
evidence: No source found for his doctorate or supervisor. Affiliated with University of Minnesota; co-edited 'The Mental Patient' (1968) with Norman Denzin.
notes: approx_phd_year 1942 looks too early. Denzin's PhD was Iowa 1966, so Spitzer was probably Denzin's Iowa contemporary or teacher; possibly an Iowa PhD. Unverified.

name: Florence Weber
evidence: Sudoc: 'Le travail à coté : étude de pratiques ouvrières en milieu rural' / Florence Weber ; sous la direction de Gérard Althabe [thèse], 1986.
notes: The input institution (NYU Graduate School of Business Administration) is wrong; she is the French sociologist and anthropologist (ENS/EHESS). Known students Cartier, Laferté and Gollac confirm the identity.

name: Lucien Goldmann
evidence: 'completed his PhD in philosophy in 1945 under the supervision of Karl Dürr' (cites Martin Jay, Marxism and Totality, pp. 305-06). Thesis on Kant.
notes: Single source (Wikipedia citing Jay). He was Piaget's assistant (employer, not advisor). His later Sorbonne doctorat ès lettres (Le Dieu caché, 1956) was not checked.

name: Gary Rhoades
evidence: CV: Ph.D. (1981), Department of Sociology, University of California, Los Angeles. No chair or advisor listed.
notes: He worked with Burton R. Clark (UCLA), but no source names Clark as dissertation chair. Do not confuse him with Gary Rhoades the Colorado State basketball player (Wikidata Q100912116).

name: Keith Larick
evidence: Found only as a dissertation chair at University of La Verne and Brandman/UMass Global; no record of his own doctorate or advisor.
notes: Brandman profile page could not be fetched (domain is defunct).

name: François Bourricaud
evidence: Doctorat ès lettres 1961: main thesis 'Esquisse d'une théorie de l'autorité', complementary thesis 'Changements à Puno' (IHEAL). No director named.
notes: This was a pre-1968 thèse d'État, so it may have had no formal director, but no source says so; no_doctoral_advisor was not used.
